Write an employer-facing cover letter tailored to this job. Use only candidate facts from the source. Preserve contribution level, shared results, dates, credential status and academic/project context. Do not turn job requirements into candidate history. Choose the strongest relevant evidence, retain useful concrete detail, and write clear natural professional English. Make a focused case through one or two relevant examples rather than reciting the résumé. Avoid generic praise and invented motivation. Use 2–4 paragraphs, at most 320 words, a salutation and signoff.

paragraphs: I am applying for the Junior Data Analyst position at Example C05 Services. I completed a Data Analytics diploma at Example Technical College in 2026, with training in Python pandas, SQL joins, Power BI, and data-quality checks.

In a three-student 2026 course project, I helped develop a Transit Delay Dashboard using public transit data. I cleaned the dataset in Python, identified duplicate journey identifiers before joining route tables, and built the team’s Power BI view comparing median delay by route and weekday. To make the analysis transparent, the report excluded cancelled trips and stated that limitation beside the chart. I also presented the team’s cleaning decisions to the class. This was coursework and was not deployed by a transit agency.

My retail experience has also required careful checking of operational information: at Example Corner Market, I checked shelf prices against the till file and reported discrepancies to the shift manager. I would bring the same attention to data quality and clear communication to your team.
